title: Systems of First-Order ODEs via Eigenvalues & Vector Spaces
subtitle: The course ends with two applications. First: solving coupled first-order differential equations using eigenvalues — the system is written in matrix form, eigenvalues and eigenvectors are found, and the general solution is a linear combination of exponential terms. Second: a brief introduction to vector spaces, linear algebra of matrices, and how it all connects to the rest of the course.

items: Linear Algebra of a matrix (LA of M)
Solve the system f₁'(x) = 2f₁(x) − 5f₂(x), f₂'(x) = f₁(x) − 4f₂(x) where f₁(0)=1 and f₂(0)=0. (2019/2020 Q2, 20 marks)
Find the eigenvalues of the system matrix and use them to write the general solution as a sum of exponential vector terms.
Apply initial conditions to find the particular solution.
